title.narrative: Output 2.1. Increased capacity of Member States to ratify international labour standards

description.narrative:
Bangladesh ratified the Protocol of 2014 to the Forced Labour Convention, 1930 by depositing the instrument of ratification on 20 January 2022. Bangladesh ratified the Minimum Age Convention, 1973 (No. 138) by depositing the instruments of ratification on 22 March 2022.
ILO provided technical assistance and consultations to MoLE to understand and present the flexibility closure of Convention No.138 and to prepare instruments of ratification of Convention No.138 and Protocol of 2004 to Convention No.29. ILO organized two workshops to conduct a rapid assessment of compliance of the Convention No.138 and Protocol of 2004 to the Convention No. 29 with national laws and practices, identified gaps and proposed recommendations. Based on the rapid assessments results, ILO prepared a brief note on necessary legislative changes to improve compliance in the course of the Labour Law reform.

description.narrative: DWCP 2022 – 2026 includes numerous references to the need to implement measures recommended by the ILO supervisory bodies, including at the output level. DWCP Priority 3 “ILS and rights at work promoted, labour market governance strengthened, and social dialogue enhanced” includes references to the implementation of the ILO supervisory bodies. Output 3.1 is “Increased ratification and implementation of international labour standards to improve labour rights in the world of work, with particular focus on ILO supervisory bodies’ recommendations”. ILO developed the draft DWCP and ensured the provisions referring to the implementation of the recommendations of the ILO supervisory bodies are included. ILO participated in the development of the UNSDCF to ensure these measures will be incorporated into the UNSDCF.

description.narrative: Existing national tripartite dialogue was strengthened to discuss ILS-related matters. A Consultation on the reports to the CEACR was conducted for the first time in Bangladesh in August 2023. National tripartite consultations were conducted in September 2022 and May 2022 on the CEACR comments on Conventions Nos. 87, 98, and 81 based on the Technical Note, prepared by the ILO, to discuss legislative reforms needed to improve compliance with C87, C98, C81 (based on the Article 24 complaint). National tripartite consultations were conducted in August 2023 on the ratification of up-to-date Conventions instead of outdated Conventions, based on the results of the SRM TWG work. Tripartite workshop will be conducted in September 2023 to plan next steps. Tripartite workshops were conducted to conduct rapid assessment of compliance of national legislation and policies with Convention No.138 and Protocol 29, and plan next steps to improve compliance with these standards. Trade union ILS committee (TU-ILS Committee) was established in May 2022 by trade unions to coordinate work on ILS ratification campaigns, prepare TU’s observations to the CEACR and coordinate work on legal and policy reforms to improve compliance with ILS. TU-ILS Committee and Bangladesh Employers’ Federation (BEF) submitted observations to the CEACR on C81, C87, C98, C144, C100, C107, C149 in 2022. They are preparing and will submit observations on the 2023 reports to the CEACR. ILO organized tripartite workshops in May 2022 and in May 2023 to strengthen the capacity of the MoLE and social partners to prepare informative reports to the CEACR, responding to the comments of the supervisory bodies. ILO provided technical assistance to organize National tripartite consultations on the reports to the CEACR in August 2023. ILO prepared Technical Note on Conventions Nos.87, 98 and 81 and organized presentation of the Technical Note at the tripartite workshop in September 2022 and supported, including technically, tripartite discussion of the Technical Note at the meeting of the Working Group of the Labour Law Reform Committee in May 2023. ILO supported and provided technical assistance to facilitate National tripartite consultations in August 2023 on the ratification of up-to-date Conventions instead of outdated Conventions, based on the results of the SRM TWG work. ILO organized tripartite workshops in September 2022 and provided technical assistance to conduct rapid assessment of compliance of national legislation and policies with Convention No.138 and Protocol 29. ILO supported capacity-building of members of the TU-ILS Committee through a serios of trainings in 2022 and 2023 on issues related to ILO supervisory system, reporting on ratified and unratified instruments to the CEACR, Technical Note and labour law reform and other. Nine representatives from Bangladesh (tripartite) participated in the ITC International Labour Standards Academy (Asia and the Pacific) in May 2022.

description.narrative: The Ministry of Labour and Employment (MoLE) submitted reports due in 2022 (C081, C087, C100, C107, C111, C149) before 1 September 2022 and provided replies to the comments of the ILO supervisory bodies. MoLE submitted reports due in 2023 on C027, C032, C081, C087, C098, C1444, C185 responding to the comments of the ILO supervisory bodies before the 1 September deadline. ILO organized three workshops in May 2022 and a workshop in May 2023 to strengthen the capacity of the Ministry of Labour and Employment (MoLE) officials and social partners to prepare informative reports to the CEACR, responding to the comments of the supervisory bodies. ILO facilitated and provided technical assistance to prepare 2022-2023 Annual work plan for the Government of Bangladesh to fulfil reporting obligations. ILO provided consultations in 2022 and in 2023 to the MoLE and Ministry of Shipping (MOS) officials to discuss the development of the reports to the CEACR and help with drafting the informative reports. Nine representatives from Bangladesh (tripartite) participated in the ITC International Labour Standards Academy (Asia and the Pacific) in May 2022. One representative of Bangladesh (MoS) participated in the ITC training “Reporting on the MLC, 2006” in March-June 2022.
